/**
 * HomeLog — a personal health diary app. Everything here is patient-generated: the patient (or a
 * device paired to the patient's phone) is the only source. No clinician has reviewed any of it.
 *
 * HomeLog publishes two kinds of item, both using the entry type `HomeLogEntry`:
 *
 * 1. **Day page.** One item per calendar day (on the phone's clock) that has at least one entry.
 *    Published at the first sync after that day ends. Holds that day's BP readings, glucose readings,
 *    dose-log entries and diary notes. The envelope `effective` is the bare date (`2024-10-31`).
 *    If the patient later edits or deletes anything on that day, HomeLog publishes a new day page that
 *    `supersedes` the old one and restates the whole day.
 *
 * 2. **My Medicines list.** One item each time the patient saves their medicine list. Holds one
 *    `my_med` entry per medicine on the list, including ones marked stopped. Each save restates the
 *    whole list and `supersedes` the previous list item. `effective` is the date of the save.
 *
 * Narrative: on a day page, the narrative is the patient's diary notes for the day, verbatim, one
 * paragraph per note. HomeLog adds only the bold time label at the start of each paragraph; the words
 * inside the `<ref>` span are exactly what the patient typed (spelling and all). Readings and dose-log
 * entries have no narrative. A My Medicines list item has a one-line narrative generated by the app
 * ("My Medicines, saved 2 May 2026").
 *
 * Times: HomeLog stores **wall-clock time as shown on the phone, with no UTC offset and no time-zone
 * name** (`"2024-10-31T08:20"`). The app does not know which time zone the phone was in. To place a
 * reading on a timeline you need the patient's time zone from somewhere else. Envelope `recorded`
 * values are server times in UTC and do carry an offset.
 *
 * Medicine names are whatever the patient typed or picked; they are not checked against any
 * prescription. A self-reported list can differ from every clinic's list, and that is the point of it.
 */

/** One entry on a HomeLog day page or My Medicines list. */
export type HomeLogEntry = BpReading | GlucoseReading | DoseLog | DiaryNote | MyMed;

/**
 * Local wall-clock date-time as shown on the patient's phone, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, no seconds, no
 * offset, no zone. Not UTC. See the module comment.
 */
type LocalDateTime = string;

/** A home blood pressure reading. */
export interface BpReading {
  type: 'bp_reading';

  /** When the cuff took the reading (cuff clock, synced to the phone), or when the patient says it was taken if typed. Local wall time. */
  measured_at: LocalDateTime;

  /** Systolic pressure, mmHg. */
  systolic_mmhg: number;

  /** Diastolic pressure, mmHg. */
  diastolic_mmhg: number;

  /** Pulse rate from the cuff, beats per minute. Absent when typed in and the patient left it blank. */
  pulse_bpm?: number;

  /**
   * How the reading got into HomeLog.
   * - 'cuff_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth cuff. Values are exactly what the cuff measured.
   * - 'typed': typed in by the patient (e.g. cuff not paired, or a reading taken elsewhere such as a
   *   pharmacy kiosk). Typos happen; the patient may later fix them, which produces a superseding day page.
   * A patient who types in a reading the cuff also synced produces two entries for one measurement;
   * HomeLog does not detect this.
   */
  entry_method: 'cuff_sync' | 'typed';

  /** Which arm, if the patient set it in the cuff profile. Absent means not recorded. */
  arm?: 'left' | 'right';
}

/** A home blood glucose reading from a fingerstick meter. */
export interface GlucoseReading {
  type: 'glucose_reading';

  /** When the meter took the reading (meter clock), local wall time. Meter clocks drift; HomeLog does not correct them. */
  measured_at: LocalDateTime;

  /**
   * The number shown on the meter, in `unit`. HomeLog does **not** convert: the value is in whatever
   * unit the meter was set to display at the time.
   */
  value: number;

  /**
   * The meter's display unit at the time of this reading, as reported by the meter.
   * - 'mg/dL': milligrams per decilitre (US convention).
   * - 'mmol/L': millimoles per litre (1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL).
   * The unit is a meter setting, so it **can change partway through one patient's history** (for
   * example a meter bought abroad, or a setting changed later). Always read it per reading.
   */
  unit: 'mg/dL' | 'mmol/L';

  /**
   * Set when the meter showed "HI" or "LO" instead of a number. `value` then holds the meter's limit
   * (600 mg/dL / 33.3 mmol/L for HI; 20 mg/dL / 1.1 mmol/L for LO), not a measurement.
   * Absent on ordinary readings.
   */
  out_of_range?: 'HI' | 'LO';

  /**
   * Meal marker the patient pressed on the meter. Absent if none was pressed.
   * - 'fasting': first reading of the day before eating.
   * - 'before_meal': before a meal other than breakfast-fasting.
   * - 'after_meal': about 2 hours after a meal (patient's judgment).
   * - 'bedtime': at bedtime.
   */
  meal_marker?: 'fasting' | 'before_meal' | 'after_meal' | 'bedtime';

  /**
   * How the reading got into HomeLog.
   * - 'meter_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth meter.
   * - 'typed': typed in by the patient, who also picks the unit. Same duplicate caveat as BP.
   */
  entry_method: 'meter_sync' | 'typed';
}

/**
 * A dose the patient logged as taken or skipped. Patients log what they choose to log; most people
 * log only some medicines (often just insulin), so **the absence of a dose-log entry does not mean a
 * dose was missed**.
 */
export interface DoseLog {
  type: 'dose_log';

  /** When the patient says they took (or decided to skip) the dose. Local wall time. */
  at: LocalDateTime;

  /** HomeLog's id for this medicine on the patient's My Medicines list. Stable across list saves; matches `MyMed.homelog_med_id`. */
  homelog_med_id: string;

  /** The medicine's name as shown on the patient's list at the time (copied, for readability). */
  med_name: string;

  /**
   * - 'taken': the patient took it.
   * - 'skipped': the patient deliberately did not take it. See `skip_reason`.
   */
  status: 'taken' | 'skipped';

  /** Amount taken, in `amount_unit`. Absent when the patient did not enter it (common for tablets). */
  amount?: number;

  /**
   * Unit for `amount`, from a fixed app list.
   * - 'units': insulin units (UCUM `[iU]`).
   * - 'tablets': number of tablets or capsules; the strength is on the My Medicines entry.
   * - 'puffs', 'mL': as named.
   * Present exactly when `amount` is present.
   */
  amount_unit?: 'units' | 'tablets' | 'puffs' | 'mL';

  /** Patient's free-text reason for a skip. Present only on some 'skipped' entries. */
  skip_reason?: string;
}

/**
 * A diary note the patient typed. The patient's words are in the day page's narrative, inside the
 * `<ref>` span whose id equals this entry's id. The payload holds only the tags the patient picked.
 */
export interface DiaryNote {
  type: 'diary_note';

  /** When the patient wrote the note (not necessarily when the symptom started). Local wall time. */
  written_at: LocalDateTime;

  /**
   * Symptom tags the patient picked from HomeLog's list. Empty when the note is not about a symptom.
   * The list (fixed in this schema version): 'nausea', 'vomiting', 'diarrhea', 'poor_appetite',
   * 'dizzy', 'tired', 'short_of_breath', 'swelling', 'headache', 'cough', 'pain', 'low_mood', 'other'.
   * Tags are the patient's own choice, not a diagnosis; the note text usually says more.
   */
  symptom_tags: Array<
    | 'nausea' | 'vomiting' | 'diarrhea' | 'poor_appetite' | 'dizzy' | 'tired' | 'short_of_breath'
    | 'swelling' | 'headache' | 'cough' | 'pain' | 'low_mood' | 'other'
  >;

  /** Patient-rated severity, 1 (barely noticeable) to 5 (worst I've felt). Absent when not rated or no symptom tags. */
  severity?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
}

/** One medicine on the patient's self-reported My Medicines list. */
export interface MyMed {
  type: 'my_med';

  /** HomeLog's id for this medicine on the list. Stable across saves of the list. */
  homelog_med_id: string;

  /** The name as the patient entered it: brand, generic or nickname ("water pill"). Not normalized. */
  name: string;

  /**
   * Set when the patient picked the name from HomeLog's drug search instead of typing it. `rxnorm` is
   * the RxNorm concept the search result was linked to (ingredient + strength + form when the patient
   * picked a specific product, otherwise just an ingredient). Absent for typed names.
   */
  picked_from_search?: { rxnorm: string; display: string };

  /** Strength as the patient wrote it, free text (e.g. "500 mg", "100 units/mL pen"). Absent if left blank. */
  strength_text?: string;

  /** How the patient says they take it, free text, in their words. May disagree with the prescription. */
  how_i_take_it?: string;

  /**
   * Whether the patient is taking it now, by their account.
   * - 'taking': currently taking (including "as needed" medicines they still use).
   * - 'stopped': no longer taking. The patient keeps stopped medicines on the list as history.
   * HomeLog has no "paused" status; patients usually mark a paused medicine 'stopped' and explain in
   * `note`, or leave it 'taking'.

content.text:
I revised `out/transform.ts` to fix both findings. The harness type-checks and runs it on the samples. I didn't re-run the two feedback patients, so neither fix has been checked against them directly.

- **Levothyroxine dose:** The old code overrode the patient's typed strength ("75 mg") with the picked product's strength ("0.075 MG"), which gave 75 mcg. The expected output keeps the strength as the patient typed it, so I removed that correction. Dose now comes from `strength_text` as written.
- **Kerendia ingredient:** Kerendia wasn't in my brand table, so the ingredient came out empty. I added Kerendia → finerenone and about 40 other common brand names (Entresto, Brilinta, Mounjaro, Coumadin and similar). I also added a few more generics to the known-ingredient list, including finerenone. Brands still missing from the table will leave the ingredient empty.

One thing I left alone: a typed strength under 1 mg (for example "0.075 mg") is still converted to mcg. The feedback gave no case for or against that.
